audit.whatIsWrong: Unstable Matter is only ever called "his W slam", and nothing anywhere states that it deals a percentage of maximum health.
audit.why: This is the interaction that decides the matchup and it is absent. Riot's text: Unstable Matter "deals a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage", on a flat 5-second cooldown. Tahm Kench is the worst possible target for that — his build (Heartsteel), his grey health conversion and his passive damage all scale off maximum health, so every point of HP he stacks makes Zac's cheapest, most frequent ability hit harder. The text currently promises the opposite, that stacking into a tank brawl favours him.
audit.corrected: Unstable Matter is percent-max-health magic damage on a flat 5s cooldown. Buy magic resist alongside the health, not just more health.

audit.whatIsWrong: Zac's passive is called the "Blob passive" throughout — "deny his passive blob pickup", "deny his Blob passive healing", "Sustain through poke using Blob passive".
audit.why: The passive is Cell Division. More importantly, the half the text never mentions is the half that matters most for an all-in: on taking fatal damage Zac splits into four bloblets and REVIVES if any survive, on a five-minute cooldown. A Tahm Kench who spends Devour and three stacks to win a fight, then walks away, has not killed him. That is a completely different decision than the one the current text describes.
audit.corrected: Cell Division: shed chunks heal him when reabsorbed, and on death he splits into four bloblets and revives if any live — 5 minute cooldown. Kill the blobs.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text says "Zac's R (Let's Bounce) becomes a point-and-click multi-knock-up".
audit.why: Let's Bounce! is not point-and-click. Riot's text: "Zac bounces four times, knocking up enemies hit and slowing them." It is a series of four landing zones you can read and step out of, on a 120/105/90s cooldown. Calling it point-and-click tells the player it is undodgeable and removes the only counterplay there is, which is watching the bounce arcs.
audit.corrected: Four bouncing knock-ups with visible landing spots, 120/105/90s — sidestep the arcs rather than trying to outrun the chain.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid, content.late, whys[4], spikes[1].text and wants.you[2] build the entire level-6 plan around "Abyssal Voyage" — spikes[1].text goes as far as "roam mid or bot while Zac is stuck top with no teleport equivalent".
audit.why: Abyssal Voyage is Tahm Kench's removed pre-2020 W. There is no global in the live kit; the W is Abyssal Dive, a 1000-1200 range knockup on 21/20/19/18/17s. An entire strategic plan — skip the lane, roam, translate a stalemate into map pressure — rests on an ability that does not exist, and the player who follows it simply loses the wave for nothing.
audit.corrected: Level 6 gives Devour, a duel and peel tool. There is no roam button; the lane is won by holding Devour for his engage.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early, whys[2] and wants.you[0] describe "stun into Devour" / "stun and Devour Zac" off one set of three stacks.
audit.why: Riot's Tongue Lash text: at 3 stacks the target is stunned and the stacks are CONSUMED. Riot's passive: three stacks are the requirement to Devour. One charge, two spenders. Against Zac the right spender is Devour — it is what denies him the window to reabsorb his Cell Division chunks, which a brief stun does not.
audit.corrected: Three stacks is one charge. Spend it on Devour to deny the blob pickups, not on the stun.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (Riot Data Dragon 16.15.1) — P and Q descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer correctly identifies Elastic Slingshot as matchup-defining but gives no cooldown, and no number appears anywhere in either layer.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9s — a very long cooldown at rank 1 and the whole reason Zac's lane is punishable early. Sidestepping one sling at level 3 buys twenty seconds of free stacking. Unstable Matter by contrast is a flat 5s and Stretching Strikes is 14/12.5/11/9.5/8s, so those are not windows at all. Without the numbers the player cannot tell which whiff is worth punishing.
51.79% over 475 games — the smallest sample in my slice but still a clear even-to-slightly-favoured read, and the chart (Tahm Kench 2, Skill 5) matches that. No change needed.

edits.before: Tongue Lash has range on everything Zac can do at Level 1 — he has no poke tool and his E sling is obvious telegraphed animation. Fire Q early and often to slow him off CS and start stacking An Acquired Taste. He will try to E behind you to break your stack rhythm and displace you from the wave; watch for the windup and sidestep, because landing in his W slam without three stacks means you eat damage and he heals a blob back. At three stacks the stun is your actual threat — if he slings in close, stun into Devour removes him from the fight and lets you reset the wave cleanly.
edits.after: Tongue Lash has range on everything Zac can do at Level 1 — he has no poke tool and his Elastic Slingshot is an obvious telegraphed animation. Fire Q early and often to slow him off CS and start stacking An Acquired Taste. He will try to sling behind you to break your stack rhythm; watch for the windup and sidestep, because Unstable Matter deals a percentage of your MAXIMUM health every 5s, which punishes the exact HP stacking your kit is built on. At three stacks spend them on Devour rather than the stun, which consumes all three.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are where this lane becomes genuinely even: Zac's E sling has full range and he can engage from angles that interrupt your stack-building, while you have no ultimate to reposition with yet. Play for wave control rather than kills — shove to tower and deny his passive blob pickup by standing over dead minion positions after you poke him. At Level 6, the calculus shifts back in your favor: Abyssal Voyage is more valuable here than Zac's Let's Bounce in a solo lane, so use the R to roam rather than match his engage in a trade you cannot decisively win.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are where this lane becomes genuinely even: Zac's E sling has full range and he can engage from angles that interrupt your stack-building, while you have no ultimate yet. Play for wave control rather than kills — shove to tower and deny his Cell Division blob pickups by standing over them after you poke him. At Level 6 the calculus shifts back in your favour: Devour answers his engage better than Let's Bounce! answers yours in a solo lane, so hold it for the moment he commits rather than matching him blow for blow.

edits.before: At two items this lane is a split between who has more team-fight value, and Zac's Let's Bounce multi-knock-up in grouped fights is genuinely threatening in ways your Devour cannot mirror at scale. Play to your kit's strengths: peel your carries with Devour, hard-engage their squishies when your three-stack stun is preloaded, and use Abyssal Voyage to arrive at fights with your CC ready rather than burned. Zac is not a hard scaler but he is a better engage initiator — stay aware of where he is before every objective fight so you are not caught repositioning when he bounces.
edits.after: At two items this lane is a split between who has more team-fight value, and Zac's Let's Bounce! multi-knock-up in grouped fights is genuinely threatening in ways your Devour cannot mirror at scale. Play to your kit's strengths: peel your carries with Devour, and remember Cell Division revives him from four bloblets on a five-minute cooldown, so killing him once may not stick unless the blobs die too. Zac is not a hard scaler but he is a better engage initiator — know where he is before every objective fight so you are not caught repositioning when he bounces.

notes: The two facts that most change how this lane is played were both absent: Unstable Matter deals percent MAXIMUM health on a flat 5s cooldown, which directly punishes Tahm Kench's own health scaling and inverts the entry's "win the attrition war by stacking" advice; and Cell Division revives Zac from four bloblets on a five-minute cooldown, so a won all-in can un-win itself. Both are in the kit file and in _missing-interactions.json. Also: the packet's three suspectNames here are false positives, except that "Let's Bounce" really is missing its exclamation mark — trivial next to the point-and-click claim in the same sentence, which is the actual error.
